chunks: And that which was narrated - Zayd ibn al-Jahm al-Hilali said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

about a man who marries a woman and marries his son to her daughter, he said: 'If the daughter was already married to him before he married her (the father), there is no harm.' These two reports are to be understood as indicating a type of dislike (karahah) rather than prohibition (hadr), because the causes of prohibition are known and none of them are present here. So when these two reports came, we interpreted them as indicating dislike so that the reports would not contradict each other.
And that which indicates what we said, that the meaning is dislike rather than prohibition, is what was narrated:

key_terms.الْكَرَاهِيَةُ: Dislike or mild disapproval in legal context, less severe than prohibition

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a man marrying a woman while his son maries her daughter in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi resolves the apparent tension in the narrations by interpreting the ruling as *karahah* (dislike) rather than *haram* (prohibition), noting that the specific causes for strict prohibition are absent. This approach preserves the consistency of the hadith corpus by avoiding contradiction, a hallmark of Shia usul al-fiqh methodology in reconciling seemingly conflicting reports.
